headline: High-risk workspace overlap: Windsurf’s broad filesystem/MCP/tooling can conflict with LangChain4j-driven workflows, while prompt-injection and leakage are limited by LangChain4j’s no-egress profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LangChain4j has no declared shared channel, but Windsurf exposes clipboard, workspace files, and MCP/tool use, so if LangChain4j outputs are copied into the IDE or read from shared files, prompt injection becomes plausible. The pathway is interaction-based and not blocked by either profile; uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF LangChain4j outputs are pasted into Windsurf prompts or saved into workspace files that Windsurf reads, injection is possible.
IF Windsurf is configured to ingest MCP/file content as instructions, attacker-controlled text can steer tool use.
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of untrusted model output into Windsurf prompts.
Keep LangChain4j outputs in a separate, read-only folder.
Require explicit provenance labels on files before Windsurf reads them.
Turn off auto-execute in Windsurf.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization/provenance filtering between the agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: LangChain4j advertises no network egress, which limits outbound leakage, but Windsurf reads workspace files, uses MCP, and has broad egress. If both touch the same files, sensitive source or open-file content can flow from LangChain4j-adjacent work into Windsurf outputs or external calls. This is a default workspace risk, not a provably blocked one.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace files, Windsurf can read and transmit file contents.
IF LangChain4j is used to process sensitive local files that Windsurf also opens, those contents can leak through Windsurf's egress.
mitigations: Separate sensitive files into a workspace Windsurf cannot access.
Disable Windsurf network access for sensitive sessions.
Use redacted copies for any shared files.
Review MCP servers before enabling them.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Windsurf can write the filesystem, modify git state, and shares state via local filesystem across instances; LangChain4j is a framework that can be embedded in workflows that also touch files. If both are pointed at the same repo, concurrent writes and git mutations can collide without locking. The conflict is plausible in default developer setups and can corrupt work.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository or workspace directory, file races can occur.
IF Windsurf auto-executes commands while LangChain4j-driven automation edits the same git state, conflicts can corrupt commits.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Disable Windsurf auto-execute.
Use git branches per agent.
requires-engineering: add file-locking or orchestration locks.

D_cascading_error.rationale: LangChain4j can generate outputs that Windsurf may treat as actionable context, and Windsurf has command execution plus MCP access. If Windsurf accepts those outputs without verification, a mistaken or malicious suggestion can cascade into edits or commands. The pair does not prove full automation, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF Windsurf uses LangChain4j-produced text as authoritative instructions, errors can propagate into tool actions.
IF auto-execute is enabled, a bad upstream output can trigger irreversible edits or commands.
mitigations: Require human review before executing generated commands.
Disable auto-execute.
Add a verification step before commits or shell actions.
Keep LangChain4j outputs as suggestions only.
requires-engineering: implement structured validation of upstream outputs.

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency or regulated-data mismatch is evidenced. LangChain4j is open-source with no declared data classes, while Windsurf handles source code/open files and model-provider keys; the pair does not itself show PHI, EU PII, or retention conflicts. Because the relevant compliance surfaces are under-specified, only a low residual gap is justified.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is placed into Windsurf workspaces, compliance review is required.
IF Windsurf's model-provider routing sends regulated content to a non-approved region, a policy breach can occur.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared workspaces.
Use de-identified samples.
Review Windsurf provider routing before use.
Restrict secrets to approved vaults.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls.
